title: Axolotl Commander — a keyboard-driven two-panel file manager for macOS
description: A free, open-source two-panel file manager for macOS, driven by the keyboard, in the spirit of Total Commander and Salamander. A native Mac app for macOS 15 and later.
ogImageAlt: Axolotl Commander icon next to the app window with two file panels.
claim: A keyboard-driven two-panel file manager for macOS.
sub: Two panels, everything from the keyboard, and a quick look at any file with F3. A native Mac app in the spirit of Total Commander and Salamander.
note: Free and open source · GPL-3.0 · macOS 15 Sequoia or later · Apple silicon and Intel
shotAlt: Axolotl Commander: two panels with path bars, tabs, marked files and the function key bar.
features: Two panels, all from the keyboard.
Tabs, F-key commands, and every shortcut can be remapped.
Copy, move, rename, links — deleting goes to the Trash, and nearly 700 automated tests guard your data.
Text and hex viewer, Quick Look, side-by-side comparison of files and whole folders.
ZIP, 7z and tar open like ordinary folders.
SFTP, FTP/FTPS and network shares, passwords in the Keychain.
Swift and AppKit, Trash, Quick Look, Finder tags. English and Czech.
why: For years I used Salamander on Windows: two panels, everything from the keyboard, a quick look at a file with F3, comparing folders, archives and FTP as ordinary folders. Nothing on the Mac felt like that. Axolotl Commander is an attempt to have the same on the Mac — as a real macOS app, not a ported Windows program.
aiH: Built with AI, in the open
aiLead: A human decides, the AI writes the code, the specification is the source of truth.
aiBody: Axolotl Commander is written by the AI assistant Claude Code, following specifications agreed on by the maintainer first. Every feature starts as a public spec made with GitHub Spec Kit — user stories, acceptance scenarios, edge cases — and only then is planned, coded and tested.
steps: User stories, acceptance scenarios, edge cases.
Nothing is planned or coded until the maintainer agrees.
The AI writes the plan, the code and automated tests.
Spec stays the source of truth
Changes are recorded in the spec first, so code and spec never drift apart.
warn: Early development software, without warranty. Data safety comes first, but please keep a backup (Time Machine).
